The two-tone steel and 18K yellow gold construction defined luxury watchmaking in the 1980s, and the Santos was at the forefront of that trend. The crisp white dial with Roman numerals and yellow gold bezel create a look that is unmistakably Cartier. The case wears exceptionally well, offering a distinct presence without being oversized. An Original And Well Preserved Piece This Santos is an honest example from its era. The case, dial, crown, and two-tone bracelet are all original to the watch. The signature white dial with Roman numerals is clean and legible. The steel and gold bracelet is well-preserved and maintains its classic structure. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. A Design Icon For Any Collection The Santos works because its design is foundational. It has a historical significance that few other watches can claim, yet it remains perfectly suited for modern wear. This two-tone version is versatile enough to be worn in nearly any setting, offering a piece of genuine watchmaking history that is both recognizable and comfortable on the wrist. It is an ideal choice for someone who values design heritage over fleeting trends.

title: 1963 Rolex Oysterdate Precision 6694 – Silver Dial
description: Early Oysterdate, pure and utilitarian This Rolex Oysterdate Precision from 1963 is a clean example of the model in its earlier, more stripped-back form. Manual wind, no frills, and built around clarity and proportion, it reflects Rolex’s everyday tool-watch philosophy before automatics became the norm. But this dial boasts something not often seen. Why this configuration works Early 6694s like this one carry a different character than later examples. The dagger indices and alpha hands give the dial more elegant look, while the date wheel provides utility. At 34mm, the proportions remain ideal for daily wear, sitting comfortably and reading cleanly on the wrist. It’s a watch defined by restraint rather than complication. Condition, clearly stated This one is in really good overall shape for the age. The case shows wear consistent with a watch that’s been worn, not overcorrected. The dial presents with dagger indices intact, and the hands show matching patina, which is consistent with age. Mechanically, the movement is running and keeping time well after passing by our test bench. All core components, case, dial, movement, and crown remain original. A straightforward vintage Rolex This isn’t about rarity or perfection. It’s about an honest early Oysterdate that captures why manual-wind Rolex watches remain so appealing decades later. For someone looking for a simple, historically grounded Rolex with clear design language and everyday wearability, this ref. 6694 delivers exactly that, a no-nonsense classic from an earlier chapter of the brand’s history.

title: Rolex Oysterdate Precision 6694 – Silver Dial
description: A Foundation Of The Rolex Catalog The Oysterdate Precision 6694 represents one of the purest expressions of the Rolex ethos. It combines the brand's iconic water-resistant Oyster case with a clean, legible dial and a robust manual-wind movement. For decades, this reference served as a gateway into the world of Rolex, offering the same durability and timeless design as its automatic siblings in a more mechanically direct package. It is a watch built on fundamentals, stripped of anything unnecessary. A Clean, All Original Execution This example from the 1970s is notable for its honest and cohesive presentation. The silver dial is fitted with a set of sharp Alpha hands, a detail prized by vintage collectors. The case is classic, comfortable, and a reminder of a time when subtlety was the ultimate statement.

title: 1972 Rolex Oysterdate Precision 6694 – Silver Dial
description: A straightforward Oysterdate, done the right way This Rolex Oysterdate Precision ref. 6694 from 1972 is exactly what the model was meant to be: simple, legible, and built for everyday wear. With its silver sunburst dial and manual-wind movement, it reflects a time when Rolex focused on clarity and reliability rather than excess. It’s familiar in the best sense — honest and well proportioned. Why this configuration works The silver sunburst dial gives the watch just enough texture to avoid feeling flat, catching light subtly while keeping the overall look clean. Paired with the 34mm steel case and smooth bezel, the result is balanced and easy to wear, sitting comfortably between dressy and utilitarian. The manual-wind movement and non-quickset date keep things straightforward, reinforcing the Oysterdate’s role as a practical daily Rolex rather than a statement piece. Condition, clearly stated Condition is consistent with age and use. The case shows normal wear, and the bracelet remains solid and wearable for its vintage. The dial displays spotting throughout, visible on close inspection and reflective of natural aging. The crystal is clean, and the buckle presents well for its age. It’s a dependable Oysterdate that highlights why these watches remain so appealing decades later: good design, sensible proportions, and an easy presence on the wrist. For someone looking for an honest vintage Rolex that can be worn regularly without fuss, this ref. 6694 delivers exactly that.

title: Universal Genève Polerouter – Tropical Dial
description: A Foundational Genta Design The Polerouter is the watch that launched the career of legendary designer Gérald Genta. Released in 1954, it was commissioned by Scandinavian Airlines to commemorate their pioneering flights over the North Pole, requiring a watch that could withstand the intense magnetic fields. Genta, then only 23, delivered a masterpiece of mid-century design with his signature twisted lugs and a clean, functional layout. It is one of the most important and accessible pieces from the mind that would later create the Royal Oak and Nautilus. The Beauty Of A Natural Color Shift This example is distinguished by its stunning tropical dial. The original black surface has aged over decades into a rich, varied brown, a natural process caused by long-term exposure to sunlight. This "tropicalization" is a unique and random occurrence that cannot be replicated, giving each watch its own specific character. The effect on this piece is particularly compelling, with different shades appearing depending on the light, all centered around a sharp crosshair pattern and accented by dauphine hands. It is paired with its original Universal Genève beads of rice bracelet. An Honest Vintage Timepiece The stainless steel case and dial are in great cosmetic, untouched condition. The dial's transformation from black to a deep, shifting brown is the main event. There is a scratch on the dial near the 9 o'clock position. The crown is a replacement, while all other parts are original to the watch. The original beads of rice bracelet is intact and fits up to a 7-inch wrist. As with every watch we offer, this piece has been verified as mechanically sound and is ready to wear. Wearable History This Polerouter offers an uncommon combination of historical design significance and the unique aesthetic of a tropical dial. It is a watch for someone who appreciates the story behind a timepiece and the organic beauty that only time can create. The 35mm case with its elegant twisted lugs is perfectly sized for modern wear, offering a piece of Genta's legacy that is both a conversation starter and a reliable daily companion.

title: 1965 Rolex Oysterdate Precision 6694 – Silver Dial
description: A Pure Expression Of Rolex The Oysterdate Precision 6694 was a mainstay in the Rolex catalog for decades, acting as a gateway to the brand for a generation of owners. title: 1993 Rolex Datejust 16233 - Champagne Diamond Dial
description: A Balanced Luxury Classic The Rolex Datejust 16233 is the definitive execution of the world’s most recognizable luxury watch. It is a reliable, classic Rolex that feels substantial and looks exactly how a luxury watch should.

title: IWC - Blue Dial
description: A Study In Seventies Elegance International Watch Company built its reputation on robust, over-engineered tool watches, but their dress pieces from the 1970s show a different side of the brand. This manual wind watch captures the era's shift toward sleeker, more expressive design. The blue sunburst dial was a confident and less common choice for the typically conservative Schaffhausen manufacture, offering a vibrant alternative to the standard silver and white dials of the day. The steel mesh bracelet flows directly from the case, creating a seamless, unified look on the wrist that was a hallmark of the period's style. It is a watch for someone who appreciates pure 70s design and the simple, enduring quality of a well-made movement.

title: Piaget 9151 – Blue Lapis Dial
description: An exquisite expression of 1970s haute horlogerie, this vintage Piaget reference 9151 is a rare and elegant timepiece that merges precious materials, bold design, and meticulous craftsmanship. title: Hublot MDM Diver – Black Dial

It is Hublot in its purest, most essential form. A Clean Expression Of 90s Design This example stands out for its clean, purposeful aesthetic. The 36mm steel case hits a sweet spot for modern wearability, offering a comfortable presence without the aggressive dimensions of later models. title: Franck Muller 7501 – White Arabic Dial

title: Chopard St. Moritz – Two Tone White DIal

title: Bvlgari Scuba SC38S – Black Dial

title: Baume & Mercier Tank 37059B - 18K Yellow Gold Faux Tiger Eye Dial

title: Cartier Baignoire Allongee - Sapphire Diamond Pave
description: This ultra-rare neo-vintage Cartier Baignoire Allongée is a masterpiece of elegance, rarity, and design innovation—an extraordinary reference that transcends traditional watchmaking and flirts with high jewelry territory. The depth, color variation, and vibrancy of the stones shift beautifully in the light, making this one of the most unique dials ever produced by Cartier. Its signature elongated oval case—measuring a graceful 22mm by 47mm—sits elegantly on the wrist, with its curvature allowing it to conform comfortably to nearly any wrist size. This example comes complete with an original Cartier navy blue strap and matching 18k white gold deployant clasp, a pairing that perfectly complements the deep tones of the dial while remaining classically understated. This watch has been recently serviced and is running flawlessly. It is in great and honest condition, with all parts 100% original, including the dial, case, and movement. The case retains its crisp definition, and the dial remains untouched and immaculate. This Baignoire Allongée isn’t just a rare Cartier—it’s a celebration of what makes the maison so revered: elegance, restraint, craftsmanship, and daring beauty. Whether you're a seasoned Cartier collector or someone looking to own a uniquely significant timepiece, this sapphire-dial Allongée is a trophy-level acquisition. title: Baume & Mercier – Blue Falcon Eye
description: A striking representation of 1970s luxury watchmaking, this vintage Baume & Mercier timepiece is crafted entirely in solid 18K yellow gold and features a rare and captivating blue Falcon’s Eye stone dial. The dial is the star of the show: Falcon’s Eye, also known as Blue Tiger’s Eye, is a natural variety of quartz known for its shimmering chatoyancy and deep, silky blue hue with subtle streaks of grey and silver. While Tiger’s Eye—with its warm golden tones—is more commonly seen in vintage watch dials, Falcon’s Eye is significantly rarer, especially in factory-set examples like this. Its cooler, stormy aesthetic offers a more understated, moody elegance, making it highly sought-after among collectors of hardstone dials. Complementing the dial are sharp Dauphine hands and a matching blue cabochon-set crown, enhancing the cohesion and detail of the design. All components—the case, dial, and movement—are 100% original and in excellent vintage condition, reflecting Baume & Mercier’s understated yet luxurious approach to watchmaking during this period. title: Cartier Tonneau - 18K Rose Gold

The silver guilloché dial, adorned with black Roman numerals and blued Breguet-style hands, reflects the maison’s mastery of proportion and detail. title: Chopard Onyx - Integrated Laykin & Co Stamped Retailer Signature Dial
description: A Masterclass In Eighties Opulence The 1970s and 80s were a playground for Chopard, a period where they moved away from traditional watchmaking constraints to focus on high-concept jewelry pieces that happened to tell time. This Ref. 2036 1 is a heavy hitter from that era. It features a deep, bottomless onyx dial housed in a yellow gold case, but the real draw is the "Retailer Signature" with Laykin & Co. Retailer stamps like this are historical fingerprints; Laykin & Co. was the premier luxury destination at the Fairmont Hotel in Los Angeles, catering to the Hollywood elite. Seeing their name alongside Chopard on a dial like this anchors the watch to a very specific, high-society West Coast history . Bamboo Gold And Deep Onyx The design language here is unapologetically bold. The integrated 14K yellow gold bracelet is finished in a "bamboo" style, a texture that was incredibly popular for high-end jewelry-watches during this period because of how it catches the light without looking like a standard flat link. The contrast between the organic, textured gold and the stark, sterile black of the onyx dial creates a balance that feels sophisticated rather than loud. It is a configuration that captures the exact energy of 1980s luxury . Condition And Reality The watch is in good, honest condition. The 18K yellow gold case and bezel have maintained their definition, and the integrated bracelet remains structurally sound with a total weight of nearly 100 grams, giving it a significant, high-quality presence on the wrist. The onyx dial is clean, showing no cracks or chips which is the primary concern with stone dials from this era. Mechanically, the movement is running strong after passing our test bench . Why It Works This is a piece for the collector who wants something that feels like an artifact. It sits in that perfect pocket of being a serious horological item due to the Chopard pedigree and Laykin & Co. stamp, while functioning primarily as a piece of sculptural jewelry. It works because it doesn't try to be an everyday tool; it is a specialized, era-defining statement that remains wearable today because of its refined proportions and classic color palette. It’s a distinct choice for someone who values provenance and style in equal measure .

title: Concord Year of Dragon - Enamel Dial
description: The 1-of-50 Enamel Dragon The Concord "Year of the Dragon" is a legitimate sleeper in the world of high-art horology. Hand-Painted Artistry The dial depicts a fierce, intricate dragon motif rendered in vivid enamel and accented by diamond hour markers. The 18k gold case measures 25mm x 34mm, offering a refined, rectangular silhouette that allows the artistry of the dial to be the undisputed focal point. It manages to feel both symbolic and sophisticated, providing a level of detail rarely encountered outside of bespoke commissions. Condition and Performance Verified The piece is in overall excellent vintage condition. The 18k gold case and sapphire crystal are in excellent condition, ensuring the enamel work remains protected and clearly visible. It is a healthy, verified, and exceptionally rare opportunity to own a high-level enamel dial timepiece at an accessible entry point. It represents a specific, "if you know, you know" trophy for the collector who values technical craftsmanship over brand hype. Mechanical Integrity and Provenance Unlike many decorative pieces of the era, this Limited Edition houses a manual-wind mechanical movement visible through a clear exhibition caseback. It remains fitted to its original black alligator strap and matching 18k gold buckle, preserving the original factory aesthetic. This example is especially notable for its completeness, as it is accompanied by the original papers—a critical detail for a piece with a worldwide production run of only 50 units. title: Cartier Santos Galbée - Two Tone Ivory Dial

Performance Verified Mechanically, the Cartier quartz movement is performing exactly as intended, offering the "set-it-and-forget-it" convenience that makes the Galbée such a reliable daily companion.
